O.outcome_detail: blinded academic marker score for digital health solution design

cells.quote: AI-generated responses showed progressive improvements with structured prompting and rubric integration, most notably in GPT-4 (V3), which scored 69% compared to 56% for GPT-4 (V1; Table 3).

O.outcome_detail: blinded academic marker score for digital health solution design

cells.quote: Notably, the use of the more advanced o1 model (V4) did not improve performance over GPT-4 (V3), scoring only 63%, and continued to exhibit generic recommendations and limited tailoring to the scenario.

O.outcome_detail: blinded academic marker score for digital health business case

cells.quote: The business case results similarly report o1 Preview V4 at 64% below GPT-4 V2 at 68%.
cells.note: The quoted sentence is from the wiki entry because the supplied study text is truncated before the detailed business case result.

result.effect: o1-Pro 93.0% (348/374) vs GPT-4o 88.8% (332/374); McNemar exact P=0.0015; discordant-pair OR 5.00 (95% CI 1.71–14.63)

cells.quote: Out of 374 UKMLA-style items, GPT-4o answered 332 correctly (88.8% accuracy), while o1-Pro answered 348 correctly (93.0% accuracy). McNemar’s exact test confirmed that o1-Pro’s advantage was statistically significant (P=0.0015).
cells.note: Both models answered the identical item set, supporting a paired within-item comparison.

cells.quote: o1-Pro achieved an accuracy of 90.0%, while GPT-4o reached 75.0% (Fig. 3). McNemar’s test indicated that this difference was not statistically significant (P=0.25).
cells.note: The study describes this image-based analysis as exploratory because of the small sample and low statistical power.

cells.note: This is a raw specialty-level difference; the study reports no per-specialty significance test or confidence interval.
